Normal.description: Legitimate enterprise network communications following expected statistical distributions.
Normal.soc_playbook: Continue standard telemetry monitoring; no containment action required.

techniques.name: Standard HTTP/HTTPS Traffic
techniques.description: Routine web browsing and API interactions.

Reconnaissance.description: Adversary attempting to get a listing of services running on hosts across the network through port scanning, IP sweeps, or banner grabbing.
Reconnaissance.soc_playbook:
1. Temporarily rate-limit probe source IPs on perimeter firewall.
2. Inspect ingress honeypots and verify no exposure of internal management ports (e.g. 22, 3389, 445).
3. Alert SOC tier-1 to monitor downstream connection spikes from probing IPs.

techniques.name: Network Service Discovery
techniques.description: Active scanning of ports and IP ranges using SYN probes or banner grabs.

techniques.name: Active Scanning
techniques.description: Automated vulnerability scanning against external endpoints.

techniques.name: Gather Victim Network Information
techniques.description: Enumerating DNS, IP allocation, and routing infrastructure.

Initial Access.description: Adversary attempting to gain entry into the network using external web exploits, password spraying, or SSH/RDP credential brute forcing.
Initial Access.soc_playbook:
1. Enforce automatic IP blocklists on edge WAF / fail2ban for source endpoints.
2. Invalidate compromised sessions and require multi-factor authentication re-auth.
3. Snapshot victim service logs and verify process spawning integrity.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.description: Exploiting web server vulnerabilities (e.g., SQLi, Log4j, RCE).

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.description: High-frequency password guessing against SSH, RDP, or HTTP login endpoints.

techniques.name: External Remote Services
techniques.description: Unauthorized access via unsegmented VPN or remote desktop gateways.

Execution.description: Adversary running malicious code, shells (PowerShell, Bash), or binary payloads on compromised host.
Execution.soc_playbook:
1. Isolate the compromised host endpoint from the VLAN via EDR network containment.
2. Terminate rogue child processes spawned by web servers or database daemons.
3. Collect memory dump and triage recent process injection artifacts.

techniques.name: PowerShell
techniques.description: Execution of obfuscated base64 commands and reflective DLL injection.

techniques.name: Unix Shell
techniques.description: Spawning /bin/sh or /bin/bash interactive reverse shells.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Client Execution
techniques.description: Triggering execution vulnerabilities in client software.

Persistence.description: Adversary attempting to maintain access across reboots, credential changes, or session terminations.
Persistence.soc_playbook:
1. Audit cron jobs, systemd timers, Windows Scheduled Tasks, and Registry run keys.
2. Review recently provisioned local service accounts or SSH authorized_keys.
3. Revoke newly created OAuth tokens or service principals.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task
techniques.description: Persistence established via schtasks or cron automation.

techniques.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.description: Auto-starting malware on system logon.

techniques.name: Create Account
techniques.description: Creation of rogue local administrator accounts for backdoors.

Privilege Escalation.description: Adversary trying to gain higher-level permissions (e.g. SYSTEM, root, Domain Admin) on compromised host.
Privilege Escalation.soc_playbook:
1. Audit local token manipulation, SeDebugPrivilege misuse, and kernel exploit signatures.
2. Immediately reset Domain Admin and local administrator passwords from an out-of-band console.
3. Restrict LSASS memory access via Credential Guard.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
techniques.description: Local kernel vulnerabilities (e.g. DirtyPipe, PrintNightmare) to elevate to root/SYSTEM.

techniques.name: Bypass User Account Control (UAC)
techniques.description: Bypassing Windows UAC to execute processes with elevated integrity.

Lateral Movement.description: Adversary extending access across the internal network by pivoting to adjacent hosts via SMB, RPC, RDP, or SSH.
Lateral Movement.soc_playbook:
1. Implement micro-segmentation rules blocking inter-workstation SMB (445) and RPC (135).
2. Isolate infected subnet segment at the top-of-rack switch level.
3. Hunt for Pass-the-Hash / Kerberoasting authentication anomalies across domain controllers.

techniques.name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.description: Spreading via PsExec or C$ admin share file transfers.

techniques.name: Remote Desktop Protocol
techniques.description: Interactive lateral movement using compromised administrator credentials.

techniques.name: Pass the Hash
techniques.description: Reusing NTLM password hashes across the subnet without cracking.

Command and Control.description: Adversary establishing periodic beaconing and covert control channels to an external command server.
Command and Control.soc_playbook:
1. Blackhole destination C2 IP/FQDN across DNS sinkholes and edge egress firewalls.
2. Block suspicious SSL/TLS certificates with self-signed or anomalous JA3 fingerprints.
3. Capture full packet payload on the active C2 stream for IOC extraction.

techniques.name: Web Protocols (HTTP/HTTPS)
techniques.description: Periodic beaconing disguised as standard outbound TLS traffic.

techniques.name: DNS Tunneling
techniques.description: Encoding commands and telemetry within recursive DNS TXT queries.

techniques.name: Encrypted Channel
techniques.description: Custom symmetric encryption over raw TCP/UDP sockets.

Exfiltration.description: Adversary stealing sensitive data, database dumps, or credentials and transmitting them off-network.
Exfiltration.soc_playbook:
1. Immediately sever external outbound connections from the transmitting host.
2. Enable DLP (Data Loss Prevention) containment on cloud egress gateways.
3. Triage stolen file metadata to determine regulatory breach notification scope (GDPR/DPDP).

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted/Encrypted Non-C2 Protocol
techniques.description: Massive data transfer over SFTP, mega.nz, or AWS S3 buckets.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
techniques.description: Uploading archives to external cloud storage repositories.

techniques.name: Automated Exfiltration
techniques.description: Scheduled compression and staging of confidential data.
